images.title: Tree ascent
images.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: initial video-game concept art for Ant Tree Game, based on docs/concept-main.md.
Art direction: grounded stylized realism with a painterly cinematic finish, attractive readable large shapes, credible macro-scale nature, warm brown bark and green leaves. Tree forms should feel feasible with procedural geometry and math/shader-driven surfaces: strong bark ridges and branching silhouettes, restrained microdetail. A recognizable dark reddish-brown worker ant has six legs, elbowed antennae, a segmented body and mandibles, with no human face, clothing or hands. The ant is millimetres long on an ordinary full-sized tree; preserve the enormous size difference. Scent paths, when requested, are a restrained translucent cyan gameplay visualization hugging the traversable surface, never a physical cable or magical beam.
Output: one polished landscape illustration, approximately 3:2 aspect ratio. No collage, no captions, no typography, no UI, no watermark. Avoid humanoid insects, fantasy villages, glowing mushrooms, oversized hero ants, extra limbs and excessive blur.
Primary request: show the feeling of playing a tiny ant climbing an immense tree.
Scene: a towering tree trunk seen from an ant-scale third-person camera hovering just behind and above the ant, with enough lateral offset to see its silhouette. The trunk's curvature and bark ridges recede in both directions beyond the frame; the distant ground is far below and branching limbs lead toward a sunlit canopy far above.
Subject/action: a small unladen worker ant climbs the near vertical bark at the lower foreground, all feet gripping the surface, headed toward a visible branch junction. Its body is readable but small within the overall composition.
Composition: a strong upward sweep from the tiny ant through broad climbable bark ledges to enormous branches. Preserve a stable readable camera horizon and clear depth cues rather than a disorienting roll. The trunk must feel far too wide to circle quickly. Do not shrink the tree into a miniature sapling.
Lighting/mood: dappled early daylight, awe, exploration and physical scale. A few small leaves and distant canopy shapes reinforce the enormous journey. No enemies or weapons in this image.

Lighting/mood: overcast windy daylight breaking through green canopy, dramatic natural contrast. No gore, attack wounds, weapons, text or HUD.

Primary request: exploratory late-game concept for the notes' ant-scale rocket launcher upgrades used to take out birds.
Scene: a vast tree branch near a fork in the canopy, framed from a low ant-scale third-person camera. A single six-legged worker ant stands on the bark in the foreground beneath a compact ant-sized rocket tube fixed to a minimal lightweight thorax harness, leaving its antennae, head and all legs free. The launcher is a legible tiny piece of functional mechanical equipment, about one ant body long, not a suit or humanoid rifle. A second ordinary unarmed ant may be present only as a distant scale cue.
Action: one tiny rocket has just launched from the ant's tube, a restrained white exhaust arc leading upward toward one ordinary songbird lifting away from the far branch. The bird is huge compared with the ant, with coherent natural bird anatomy. Show the bird reacting by taking flight, with no impact, gore or explosion obscuring the design.
Composition: clear readable ant/launcher silhouette in foreground, rocket trajectory carrying the eye toward the much larger bird, and enormous trunk and canopy shapes anchoring the scale. The central idea is the improbable payoff of colony progression within an otherwise grounded tiny natural world.
Lighting/mood: bright late-afternoon rim light, triumphant and slightly playful escalation, still visually consistent with the grounded environment concepts. Keep the only invented technology confined to the explicitly requested rocket upgrade. No helmets, clothing, human hands, giant ant, army, tanks, settlement, text or HUD.
